scope: Interpret retained H02 host-origin setter metadata, compare the separately established PD08 same-inode host/Simulator exposure difference, and apply retained public API/source contracts. This is not another control, collection, cleanup or full qualification audit and does not design the separately owned syscall follow-up.

h02.runtime: Native macOS 15.7.9/24G830 arm64; Xcode 26.3/17C529; MacOSX SDK 26.2.
h02.fixture_origin: One ordinary host-created file, not a PD08/PD09 Simulator inode. The frozen driver creates a private 0700 root at run_host_probe.py:330-333 and calls native.write_new; native_continuation.py:129-135 uses O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, mode0600, write/flush/fsync. There is no initial Foundation protection option or NSData Complete-creation request. The before sample is therefore ordinary/default creation; the after sample follows a failed Complete request, not successful protected-file creation.
h02.identity_checks: Both raw samples have the identical full file identity. Each contains five per-API before/after identity witnesses with descriptor_and_path_same_inode=true and a closed descriptor. The retained report's before, operation and after records match the raw records.

operation.error_limit: The template normalizes NSCocoaErrorDomain to cocoa and retains only presence/domain/code. No underlying NSError chain or POSIX errno was retained; absent evidence is not evidence of an absent underlying error. Cocoa256 must not be translated into ENOTSUP or attributed to a particular syscall.

unchanged_before_and_after.fresh_url: Dictionary/key present, until-first-authentication, no NSError; volume_support=unsupported.

Host FileManager getter is Foundation UUID39be75ac-350f-3b8c-9c10-8b2b5321ce8e/offset211688; URL getter is CoreFoundation UUIDbdc82415-a029-3463-ac49-1a792208ce00/offset520524. pd08_comparison.observation: On each identity-validated host/Simulator pair, FileManager exposes until-first-authentication on the host but omits the key in Simulator. Both readers obtain fcntl class3/errno0 and valid-bit attrlist class3. Four regular-file fresh-URL values agree until-first-authentication; directory protection URL is unrequested/N/A. Both contexts advertise unsupported volume capability with MNT_CPROTECT clear.
pd08_comparison.separation: PD08 proves a same-object API/runtime-context exposure difference within its own run. H02 instead tests a native-host mutation on a separately created file in a different run with a different filesystem ID. Their matching host versions/getter images are contextual evidence, not cross-run inode or volume identity. No H02/PD08 evidence stitching is used.

contract_interpretation: Apple's Complete contract concerns encrypted-on-disk data unavailable while locked or booting. A readable class label, a successful getter, or even an affirmative setter return would not independently demonstrate device-lock/keybag enforcement. Here the actual setter return is false.

NSURLVolumeSupportsFileProtectionKey describes whether the volume supports file data protection. The retained XNU mount.h:303 defines MNT_CPROTECT as the content-protection support advertisement. Their negative observations here must not be overwritten by a readable C/class3 label.

The retained XNU kern_descrip.c:4369-4399 returns supported va_dataprotect_class through F_GETPROTECTIONCLASS without an MNT_CPROTECT prerequisite; vfs_attrlist.c:2108-2114 exposes the same attribute with returned-valid-bit handling. Readable class3 alongside a clear capability bit is therefore not an internal contradiction. The two class-read APIs are not two independent encryption/enforcement proofs.

The retained public Swift Foundation utility's getter at225-237 uses getattrlist without a returned-attribute mask. Its setter at240-244 skips an already matching class, opens O_WRONLY at246, and at265-275 suppresses F_SET ENOTSUP when fstatfs fails OR MNT_CPROTECT is clear. Its EACCES suppression at277-280 is specifically an open failure, not every setter EACCES. These public-source paths are hypotheses, not proof of the installed macOS implementation. H02's actual FALSE/Cocoa256 does not confirm the earlier predicted YES/ENOTSUP-suppression result.

The retained Swift6.2.3 FileManager+Files.swift getter at656-665 and setter at990-1000 are guarded by !targetEnvironment(simulator) && FOUNDATION_FRAMEWORK. This offers a candidate explanation for PD08's exposure difference, not exact installed-runtime branch proof. H02 itself demonstrates that the native host public setter API can be compiled and invoked; public symbol availability does not guarantee volume capability or a successful Complete transition.

The retained XNU content_protection.h places A1/C3 definitions inside PRIVATE. Numeric labels may be interpreted as reference metadata but must not become invented public SDK mutation constants. No private/numeric setter or production fallback is proposed by this review.

established: One native-host public Complete request was rejected with FALSE/Cocoa256 on an ordinary host-created regular file; all retained post-read class metadata remained C/class3 and the volume advertised unsupported capability.
Simulator-origin file creation or a Simulator process is not necessary for this observed Complete-setting failure.

PD08 separately establishes the host/Simulator FileManager metadata-exposure difference on identical objects. Together these are evidence of a sampled host/runtime/filesystem-context limitation, not merely an application snapshot replacement issue.
not_established: The underlying syscall, errno, exact installed Foundation branch, exclusive APFS/kernel cause, or whether an approved alternate mutation API could change this class.
Universal Simulator impossibility, universal macOS/APFS class-A impossibility, or the actual protection state of unobserved production snapshots.
Encryption, device-lock/keybag enforcement, a new protection PASS, or justification for changing production storage code or weakening the strict oracle.
conclusions.qualification_boundary: Retained shipping strict0/26 and APP0/6 remain unchanged; those are carried-forward gate outcomes, not recounted by this review. H02 observes no production snapshots, is host-origin only, and cannot promote any failed runtime or Store/physical-device gate.
conclusions.physical_vs_diagnostic_boundary: Actual physical-iOS evidence is required to qualify device-lock/keybag enforcement. It has not been shown necessary merely to diagnose H02's host setter rejection or PD08's metadata discrepancy. Do not declare all remaining technical investigation physical-only.
conclusions.next_action_boundary: Do not repeat the unchanged read-only matrix or broad application matrix. Preserve the actual FALSE/error result and the lack of underlying errno. Root/protection_host separately own whether a bounded underlying-error or approved SDK syscall diagnostic is justified; this interpretation neither executes nor pre-authorizes another probe.
